high.title: Exported component consumes attacker-controlled Intent data
high.description:
Two findings in this app combine into a single exploitable path: "Exported activity UserDetailsActivity has no permission protection" and "Permission bypass in UserDetailsActivity".

Attack path:
1. Attacker starts exported UserDetailsActivity
2. Attacker provides 'path' extra in Intent
3. UserDetailsActivity constructs URI for UserDetailsContentProvider
4. UserDetailsActivity calls setResult with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION
5. Attacker receives Intent with granted URI permission
6. Attacker reads sensitive data from UserDetailsContentProvider
high.impact: The component is invokable by any app on the device and acts on the Intent it is handed without validating it, so a malicious app drives the target app's privileged behaviour with data of its choosing.
high.recommendation: Guard the component with a signature-level permission, or unexport it. Validate every Intent extra before use, and never forward a nested Intent received from a caller.

high.title: Missing permission protection in UserDetailsContentProvider
high.description: Provider "edu.ksu.cs.benign.provider.UserDetailsContentProvider" is reachable by any app on the device (android:exported="true") and declares no permission.
high.impact: Any installed app can invoke this component and whatever it does with the data it is handed.
high.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" if it is internal, or guard it with a signature-level permission and validate all input.

medium.title: Exported activity UserDetailsActivity has no permission protection
medium.description: Activity "edu.ksu.cs.benign.UserDetailsActivity" is reachable by any app on the device (Has an intent-filter and no explicit android:exported (implicitly exported)) and declares no permission. It handles userDetails. The exported UserDetailsActivity takes a 'path' extra from an Intent, constructs a URI for the UserDetailsContentProvider, and returns it via setResult with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION (flag value 1).
medium.impact: An unprivileged third-party app can bypass the 'internalRead' permission requirement of the UserDetailsContentProvider to read sensitive user data, including SSNs, by calling UserDetailsActivity via startActivityForResult.
medium.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" if it is internal, or guard it with a signature-level permission and validate all input.

medium.impact: Any application on the device that obtains the internalRead permission can extract the SSNs of users stored in the app's private data directory.

medium.title: Permission bypass in UserDetailsActivity
medium.description: The exported UserDetailsActivity allows any application to bypass the 'edu.ksu.cs.benign.permission.internalRead' permission required to access the UserDetailsContentProvider. An attacker can start this activity and provide a 'path' extra (e.g., '/user/ssn'). The activity then returns a URI pointing to the content provider via setResult() with the Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION flag (set as 1 on line 20), granting the calling application temporary read access to sensitive user data, including Social Security Numbers (SSNs).

low.title: Custom permission internalRead is weakly protected
low.description: Custom permission "edu.ksu.cs.benign.permission.internalRead" uses protectionLevel="dangerous": any installed app can request it, and gets it once the user accepts one permission prompt (at install time on Android 5.1 and lower). The custom permission 'edu.ksu.cs.benign.permission.internalRead' used to protect sensitive user data in the UserDetailsContentProvider is defined with a 'dangerous' protection level.
low.impact: Because 'dangerous' permissions can be requested by any app and granted by the user, this provides insufficient protection for highly sensitive data like SSNs.
low.recommendation: Use protectionLevel="signature" for permissions guarding internal components.

info.title: Application is debuggable in this build
info.description: android:debuggable="true" lets any user with adb attach a debugger to the process, read and modify memory, and inspect application data. The application is marked as debuggable in the manifest, allowing attackers to attach a debugger, inspect memory, and execute arbitrary code in the app's context.
info.impact: Complete compromise of the application's runtime environment, including access to all private data and the ability to bypass logic checks.
info.recommendation: Remove android:debuggable or set it to "false" for release builds.

reasons: Debuggable release build. A debuggable build is a release-pipeline defect rather than an exploitable flaw - attaching a debugger already requires ADB access to the device. Worth fixing, not worth a severity.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 27 those defaults still permit cleartext HTTP (see the cleartext finding).
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.

info.title: No screenshot protection: FLAG_SECURE is never set
info.description: Nothing in the app sets WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE, so every screen can be screenshotted or recorded and appears in the recent-apps snapshot.
info.impact: Credentials, balances or personal data on screen end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview.
info.recommendation: Set FLAG_SECURE on the windows of screens that show credentials or account data.

reasons: Screen contents not protected from capture. Without FLAG_SECURE, what a screen shows can end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview. That matters on screens showing credentials, card numbers or balances; on its own it is a hardening note.

info.title: targetSdkVersion 27 allows implicit component export
info.description: On targetSdk 27, any component with an intent-filter is exported unless it says otherwise.
info.recommendation: Raise targetSdkVersion to 31+ and declare android:exported explicitly on every filtered component.

reasons: Legacy platform behaviour from SDK levels. An SDK level is a statement about which platform defaults apply, not a defect. It is context for the findings that depend on those defaults - pair it with one of them.
warnings: Implicit export only applies below targetSdk 31; confirm the app's targetSdkVersion before treating this as exploitable.

info.description: targetSdk 27 predates API 28, where cleartext HTTP became opt-in.

reasons: Cleartext permitted by configuration. The flag permits HTTP; it does not show that anything is sent over it. Name a request that actually goes out in cleartext, and what it carries, and this is a genuine finding.
warnings: Cleartext is blocked by default from targetSdk 28; confirm the declared target and any network security config.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 22 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "edu.ksu.cs.benign". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task.
info.impact: On a device running Android 10 or lower, a malicious app can put a look-alike screen on top of this app's task, phishing credentials or keeping the real app from being shown.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.
